---
title: "Authoring and support"
---

## Start with a native export

Install STACK SymPy and AI Feedback in your Quarto project, and install SymPy in the Python environment Quarto uses:

```bash
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy
quarto add Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback
python -m pip install 'sympy==1.13.3'
```

Add the question filter to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
filters:
  - stack-sympy
```

Use a Moodle STACK export whose root is `<quiz>` and whose questions use `<question type="stack">`. Keep the normal question, input, PRT, deployed-seed, and qtest elements. Point a `stack-question` block at its XML path and exact `<name><text>…</text></name>`. The filter embeds a selected question and precomputes the requested variants when Quarto renders. The original XML remains the source of truth and can be imported back into Moodle.

```{.stack-question}
#| file: ../questions/polynomial-expansion.xml
#| question: Expand a product (form-sensitive)
#| seed: 17
#| variants: 3
#| review: true
#| feedback: true
```

Run `quarto render`, then serve the generated site over HTTP. The [README](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/stack-sympy#install-in-a-quarto-project) also covers local development setup.

The learner submits in two steps: **Validate answers** parses the current fields and displays the expression form (for example, `x+x` rather than a simplified `2*x`), then **Check answer** grades that validated response. Editing any field invalidates the preview, so the learner must validate again. This explicit check mirrors the question input verification setting and helps learners catch syntax errors before grading. The polynomial example sets `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`, so `x**2+8x+15` previews as one sum and receives full credit in its first variant.

Below a rendered question, **Show source** reveals its authored Quarto fenced block and **Show STACK source** reveals the original XML file contents. Both panels start closed; they are available for inspecting and copying a working example.

The options are `file` and `question` (required), `seed` (signed integer, default 1), `variants` (1–20, default 1), `review` (`true` or `false`, default false), and `diagnostics` (`true` or `false`, default false). `feedback: true` opts a card into the [shared AI Feedback extension](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback); cards without it need no AI dependency. Install both extensions in the same project; feedback requires AI Feedback 0.8.0+ and Quarto 1.8.27+. `context: auto` (default) uses nearby visible prose; `context: none` omits it; `context: id1,id2` includes tagged blocks such as `::: {#id1 .ai-context}` (`.ai-feedback-context` and `.math-exercise-context` are shared aliases). `feedback-language` sets the explanation language (default document `lang`). `feedback-policy` selects an existing named policy from `ai-feedback.policy-files` or page policy files. A stable `label` targets exercise-specific policy settings; otherwise the card ID is used. The shared mathematics policy (`math-exercise`) supplies the default hints and is also the YAML integration namespace for STACK cards. A fixed seed reproduces a variant within this implementation. It does not promise the same pseudo-random sequence as Moodle's Maxima backend.

Feedback uses a learner's current answer, visible question text and selected context. A preceding matching **Check answer** can contribute minimal result status, finite score; XML, source panels, teacher answers, qtests, grader configuration, grader feedback messages and answer notes are excluded. It never grades a response or replaces **Validate answers** and **Check answer**. The shared settings panel lets a learner choose copy-prompt mode or configure their own compatible provider; no API key is placed in the page. The same [explicit teaching policies](https://github.com/Erasmus-CTM/ai-feedback/blob/main/docs/feedback-policies.md) are inherited across integrations, using `math-exercise` for STACK's mathematics policy namespace.

## Choose a teaching policy

The shared `math-exercise` defaults offer four steps, ending with a worked
solution. Loading policy definitions does not select them. The example site
loads [feedback/course.yml](../feedback/course.yml) and explicitly selects its
course policy in `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
ai-feedback:
  policy-files: feedback/course.yml
  project-policy:
    math-exercise: course-mathematics
```

A policy can inherit those defaults and specialize them by name:

```yaml
# feedback/course.yml
ai-feedback:
  policies:
    course-mathematics:
      max-words: 120
      reset-on-run: true
    brief-mathematics:
      extends: course-mathematics
      max-words: 90
    two-step-practice:
      extends: brief-mathematics
      steps:
        - step-prompt: Ask one guiding question without giving a formula or answer.
        - step-prompt: Give a concise worked explanation of this task.
          allow-full-solution: true
```

Select the specialization with `#| feedback-policy: two-step-practice` on a
feedback-enabled STACK block. `#| label: rational-practice` gives it a stable
key for YAML `exercises.math-exercise` overrides. `examples.qmd` also selects
`page-policy: {math-exercise: brief-mathematics}` in its front matter. Its other
cards inherit four steps; only the selected card replaces the sequence with
two. Omitted fields inherit, while a supplied `steps` list replaces every step
and its permissions. `base-prompt` changes the continuing teaching instructions;
`step-prompt` describes one step. Use neither the retired `prompt` field nor
an authored `integrations`/`defaults` section.

Edits clear stale feedback and Check evidence while preserving hint progress.
Check resets progress by default; a selected policy can set `reset-on-run: false`
to preserve it. Selecting a different variant always restarts progress. Feedback
collects a snapshot without running validation, grading, or authored tests.

## What the adapter checks

| Supported here | Scope |
|---|---|
| Source | Moodle STACK XML `<quiz>` with named STACK questions; category and description entries are skipped. |
| Inputs | Scalar algebraic and numerical text answers, with strict syntax and `<insertstars>0</insertstars>` or `<insertstars>1</insertstars>`. Mode 0 requires `*`; mode 1 also accepts adjacent `2x`, `2(x+1)`, `(x+1)(x-1)`, and `(x+1)x`. Both keep `xy` as one symbol; whitespace alone never means multiplication. Other insertstars modes fail at import. |
| Variables | A small, safely parsed Maxima-like assignment and arithmetic subset, including `rand(n)` for seeded variants and two-integer `lcm(a,b)`. `ratsimp` preserves a common-denominator form for supported scalar expressions. |
| Scalar functions | Elementary functions include `ln` as an alias for `log`, bounded rational-polynomial `gcd(a,b)`, and real scalar `mod(a,b)`, including Maxima's `mod(x,0)=x`. Author expressions also support `num`, `denom`, `ev(expr)`, and `ev(expr,simp)`. Symbolic complex logarithms requiring branch proofs remain unsupported. |
| Tests | `AlgEquiv`, `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac`, `LowestTerms`, `NumAbsolute`, `NumRelative`, `NumDecPlaces`. The four form-sensitive tests require `sans` to name an input directly. `FacForm` also requires one polynomial variable in `<testoptions>` (a symbol or an author alias resolving to one); it checks equivalence and factorization of univariate polynomials over the rationals. Blank or syntactically malformed absolute/relative tolerances default to 0.05, while decimal places require an explicit count from 1 to 50. See the README for the expression whitelist. |
| PRTs | Acyclic node graphs with `=`, `+`, and `−` score operations, weighted response trees, branch feedback and notes. |
| Author tests | Native `<qtest>` inputs and expected PRT score, penalty, and answer note. |

This is a deliberately limited evaluator, not a replacement for Moodle STACK or its Maxima CAS. `questionsimplify=0` (`simp:false`) is accepted when any `EqualComAss` teacher form can be preserved after freezing author variables; otherwise the build rejects it. In this mode, supported `{@expression@}` CASText also preserves authored arithmetic form and groups substitutions inside existing TeX math. `EqualComAss`, `FacForm`, `SingleFrac`, and `LowestTerms` require a direct input name in `sans` to preserve the student’s written form. `FacForm` considers the written factors, including common integer content, and rejects expressions outside its bounded polynomial subset or a missing/non-symbol variable option. `SingleFrac` requires an equivalent single written fraction (or equivalent atomic answer) and excludes divisions nested in its numerator or denominator. `LowestTerms` checks reducible written integer fractions and supported denominator restrictions; it does not compare the teacher expression or factor symbolic polynomials. Build-time validation rejects unsupported author features rather than silently grading them differently. Symbolic equivalence uses SymPy transformations rather than randomized substitution. Decimal-place grading reads the literal answer so a trailing zero is meaningful. Native qtest answer notes are checked using STACK-style ordered subsequence matching, including anchored beginning/end notes and `NULL`: a terminal note can pass even if earlier PRT nodes contributed notes. The review interface and qtests help an author inspect the selected seeds, but they do not establish complete parity with all STACK configurations.

CASText also renders a scalar equality such as `{@p=ta@}` as an equation for display. `AlgEquiv` additionally supports bounded polynomial equation inputs and disjunctions, with root multiplicity retained. For example, `a=0 or b=0` matches `a*b=0`, while `a^3*b^3=0` does not. It also supports pure Boolean expressions and elementary hyperbolic functions such as `cosh` and `tanh`. See the [examples](../examples.qmd#hyperbolic-equivalence) and the README for the precise limits.

## Validate and publish

For an extension-only installation, install `sympy==1.13.3` in the Python environment used by Quarto. Run `python -m stack_sympy.cli test --file questions/polynomial-expansion.xml` after placing `_extensions/stack-sympy` on `PYTHONPATH`, then render with `quarto render`. Serve the `_site` directory through an HTTP server, including locally: `python -m http.server --directory _site 8000`. Browser grading loads Pyodide and SymPy; its first use downloads runtime packages, so it needs network access. Review the generated question and run its qtests before publishing any assessment. If a source uses features outside the supported subset, `#| diagnostics: true` displays the location of a build error in the page during authoring; remove it for production so unsupported questions fail the render.
